title: SailPoint Engineer Domain 4 questions (4.1, 4.2, 4.3)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: A team will run its first virtual appliances in the company's own AWS account. What must it do FIRST to get the VA image for EC2?
choices: Ask SailPoint Support to share the AMI with the account and region
Launch an Amazon Linux instance and install the VA packages from a repository
Subscribe to the SailPoint VA listing in the public AWS Marketplace
Download the OVA package and import it with the EC2 VM Import service
questions.answer: Ask SailPoint Support to share the AMI with the account and region
questions.explanation: For AWS, SailPoint Support shares a private AMI with the customer's account and region. Importing the vSphere package yourself is not the documented AWS path.

questions.stem: An engineer is building a VA on Hyper-V from the SailPoint VHD. Which option should be chosen on the Specify Generation screen of the New Virtual Machine Wizard?
choices: Generation 2 with Secure Boot enabled
Generation 2 with Secure Boot disabled
Generation 2 with the TPM enabled
Generation 1
questions.answer: Generation 1
questions.explanation: The documented Hyper-V build uses a Generation 1 VM with an existing virtual hard disk. Generation 2 options are not part of the SailPoint procedure.

questions.stem: A newly deployed VA on Hyper-V shows intermittent DNS failures and irregular routing. Which action does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Install the Hyper-V integration services package
Mask the waagent service and reboot the VA
Change the virtual switch from External to Internal
Add the DNS servers as entries in hosts.yaml
questions.answer: Mask the waagent service and reboot the VA
questions.explanation: Hyper-V images ship with the Azure waagent service enabled, which can cause DNS and routing issues, so it is masked. An Internal switch would cut the VA off from SailPoint and the sources.

questions.stem: An Azure administrator has extracted the SailPoint VHD to deploy a VA in Azure. Which approach matches the documented deployment?
choices: Create an Ubuntu VM and attach the SailPoint VHD to it as a data disk
Import the vSphere OVA with Azure Migrate and convert it to a VM in place
Upload the VHD to blob storage, make a managed disk, then create the VM from it
Ask SailPoint Support to share a gallery image, then create the VM from the gallery
questions.answer: Upload the VHD to blob storage, make a managed disk, then create the VM from it
questions.explanation: Azure VAs are built by uploading the VHD to blob storage, creating a managed disk and attaching it as the OS disk of a new VM. A support-shared image is the AWS process, not Azure.

questions.stem: A VMware team asks how to size a standard VA that runs no extra cluster components. Which allocation meets SailPoint's documented minimum?
choices: 2 processors, 8 GB memory and 64 GB storage
4 processors, 8 GB memory and 256 GB storage
2 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage
4 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage
questions.answer: 4 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage
questions.explanation: The minimum VA image is 4 processors, 16 GB memory and 128 GB storage. Undersizing memory leads to memory health warnings and unstable connector work.

questions.stem: An organization enables the Privileged Access Gateway component on an existing Standard VA cluster. What must the infrastructure team do?
choices: Install the gateway package on each VA from the console
Create a separate IAI Harvester cluster for the component
Add the component's extra CPU and memory to every VA in the cluster
Nothing, because cluster components run in SailPoint's cloud, not on the VAs
questions.answer: Add the component's extra CPU and memory to every VA in the cluster
questions.explanation: Each enabled cluster component raises the minimum size of every VA in the cluster, and the customer must allocate those resources. Components are delivered by SailPoint, not installed by hand.

questions.stem: Two production VAs will serve the same cluster in one data center. How should they be placed on the virtualization layer?
choices: On separate hosts so one host failure cannot stop both
On the same host so the two VAs share memory and cache
On one host behind a load balancer that splits requests between them
In one virtual machine with two network interfaces
questions.answer: On separate hosts so one host failure cannot stop both
questions.explanation: SailPoint's distribution guidance is one VA per virtual machine host, which keeps the cluster available if a host fails. Sharing a host removes that redundancy.

questions.stem: A network architect proposes putting all VAs in the DMZ because it already has internet access. What is the MOST important reason SailPoint advises against this?
choices: Connectors refuse to run when the VA's subnet is marked as a perimeter
Each VA holds the private key that decrypts source credentials
VAs cannot reach SailPoint's cloud endpoints from a DMZ network segment
SailPoint stops automatic updates for any VA that has a public address
questions.answer: Each VA holds the private key that decrypts source credentials
questions.explanation: Security is the main reason: the VA stores the RSA private key used to decrypt source credentials. Nothing technically stops a DMZ VA from reaching SailPoint.

questions.stem: A company's latency-sensitive HR database is in London and its Active Directory is in Dallas. Where should the VAs be deployed?
choices: In one cluster at headquarters, whatever the location of the sources
Near each set of sources on internal networks, one cluster per site
In the DMZ of whichever data center has the fastest internet link
In the cloud region of the SailPoint tenant, close to the tenant
questions.answer: Near each set of sources on internal networks, one cluster per site
questions.explanation: VAs should sit close to the sources they talk to because some connector APIs are latency sensitive. A source uses one cluster, so a cluster near each site gives the best performance.

questions.stem: If VAs were placed in the DMZ and still had to manage internal sources, which additional burden would MOST likely follow?
choices: More ports opened on the internal firewall from the DMZ to the sources
A second tenant to keep DMZ traffic separate from internal traffic
Inbound HTTPS rules from SailPoint to the DMZ so work can be pushed
A hardened replacement operating system image for each VA in the DMZ
questions.answer: More ports opened on the internal firewall from the DMZ to the sources
questions.explanation: A DMZ is meant for externally facing components, so reaching internal sources means opening more internal firewall ports. VAs never need inbound HTTPS from SailPoint.

questions.stem: An organization reaches its AWS VPC from its data center over a VPN, and its VAs will run in AWS to manage both cloud and on-premises sources. Which placement follows SailPoint guidance?
choices: In the region nearest to SailPoint's support organization
In us-east-1, because every VA must use that region's AWS endpoints
In the AWS region that hosts the organization's VPN network gateway
In any region, because VAs make only outbound connections
questions.answer: In the AWS region that hosts the organization's VPN network gateway
questions.explanation: Cloud VAs should be close to their targets, and with a VPN they belong in the regions hosting the network gateways. Allowing us-east-1 URLs is a firewall rule, not a placement rule.

questions.stem: A company has a production tenant and a sandbox tenant. Which VA cluster design follows SailPoint's guidance?
choices: A sandbox that borrows the production cluster through a tunnel
One shared cluster paired with both tenants to save resources
Two VAs for production and a single VA for the sandbox tenant
A separate cluster for each tenant, each with at least two VAs
questions.answer: A separate cluster for each tenant, each with at least two VAs
questions.explanation: SailPoint requires at least one production and one sandbox cluster, each with at least two VAs, so changes can be tested and updates do not cause outages. A VA pairs with one tenant only.

questions.stem: A subsidiary in a country with data residency restrictions wants a VA installed locally. What do SailPoint's contracts require?
choices: Install it in a SailPoint-approved country and handle the transfer compliance
Install the VA locally and pair it with a dedicated sandbox tenant
Install the VA locally and route all of its traffic through a network tunnel
Install the VA locally, as long as FIPS mode is enabled on it
questions.answer: Install it in a SailPoint-approved country and handle the transfer compliance
questions.explanation: Contracts bar installing VAs in countries with data residency or transmission restrictions such as Russia and China. The customer installs elsewhere and handles compliance for moving the data.

questions.stem: Sources in two isolated network segments cannot reach each other's networks. Why should the engineer create a separate VA cluster for each segment?
choices: A cluster can serve no more than one network subnet by design
Sources are billed per cluster, so splitting them lowers cost
Any VA in the cluster may take the source's requests, so all must reach it
Each VA cluster can host only one connector type at a time, so types must be split
questions.answer: Any VA in the cluster may take the source's requests, so all must reach it
questions.explanation: Requests for a source are queued to its cluster and any running VA in that cluster can take them. A VA that cannot reach the source would fail those requests.

questions.stem: An organization places primary-site and DR-site VAs in one cluster, all powered on. What is the main disadvantage of this design?
choices: Sources must be moved to the DR cluster during an outage
DR VAs far from the sources may pick up requests and add latency
DR VAs fall behind on updates because they do no work
Failover requires re-entering every source's credentials on the DR VAs
questions.answer: DR VAs far from the sources may pick up requests and add latency
questions.explanation: In the all-VAs-running strategy any VA can take a request, including distant DR VAs, so latency is the trade-off. In return, failover needs no action.

questions.stem: During a full outage of the primary data center, which HA/DR strategy keeps sources working with no administrator action?
choices: Switch clusters with a separate DR cluster powered on
A single VA in the primary site with nightly snapshots
Standby reactive VAs that are not yet in a cluster
All VAs running in one cluster across both sites
questions.answer: All VAs running in one cluster across both sites
questions.explanation: When primary and DR VAs share a cluster, the DR VAs simply keep polling and processing the queue. The other strategies need sources or VAs reassigned first.

questions.stem: A team uses a primary VA cluster and a separate DR cluster, both powered on. The primary site is lost. What work is needed before sources function again?
choices: Point each source at the DR cluster and re-enter its source credentials
Copy config.yaml from a primary VA onto each DR VA
Generate new pairing codes and pair each of the DR VAs with the tenant again
Ask SailPoint Support to fail the tenant over to DR
questions.answer: Point each source at the DR cluster and re-enter its source credentials
questions.explanation: In the switch-clusters strategy sources must be reconfigured to the DR cluster, which requires re-entering their credentials. That is hard with many sources or missing credentials.

questions.stem: Standby VAs are built and tested in a DR zone but not added to any cluster. What is the main drawback of this standby reactive strategy?
choices: The standby VAs require a load balancer to join the cluster
The standby VAs add latency to requests during normal daily operation
Recovery waits until the standby VAs join the cluster and come online
The standby VAs take production work while they are idle
questions.answer: Recovery waits until the standby VAs join the cluster and come online
questions.explanation: Standby VAs do nothing until deployed to the cluster after a disaster, so turnaround depends on how fast and how ready they are. They add no latency during normal operation.

questions.stem: A design reviewer asks for a load balancer in front of a two-VA cluster. What is the BEST response?
choices: It is required only when the cluster uses an HTTP proxy
It is required so SailPoint can push requests to one virtual IP
It is recommended so the two VAs keep their keys in sync
It is not required, because each VA polls the cluster's queue for work
questions.answer: It is not required, because each VA polls the cluster's queue for work
questions.explanation: SailPoint states a load balancer is not required: VAs pull work from the cluster's queue, which spreads it naturally. SailPoint never pushes inbound connections to the VAs.

questions.stem: A cluster has only one VA. What risk does this create when SailPoint rolls out a VA update?
choices: The cluster switches to debug logging until the update ends
Sources lose connectivity while the only VA updates and reboots
The update is held back until a second VA joins the cluster
Stored source credentials must be re-entered after every update completes
questions.answer: Sources lose connectivity while the only VA updates and reboots
questions.explanation: Updates are applied and rebooted one VA at a time, so a second VA keeps the cluster available. With one VA, its reboot is an outage.

questions.stem: Which HA/DR strategy keeps DR VAs powered on and receiving updates while ensuring they add no latency to everyday requests?
choices: Switch clusters
One cluster with DR VAs powered off
All VAs running
Standby reactive deployment
questions.answer: Switch clusters
questions.explanation: In switch clusters, the DR cluster is powered on and updated but serves no sources until failover. All VAs running can add latency; standby VAs are outside any cluster.

questions.stem: To save resources, an engineer powers off the DR VAs that are members of the production cluster. What is the MOST significant side effect?
choices: Source credentials stored for the cluster are removed after a day
The cluster is converted to a standby reactive deployment
No VA in the cluster gets software updates while any member is not connected
Production VAs begin sending their requests to SailPoint's cloud for processing
questions.answer: No VA in the cluster gets software updates while any member is not connected
questions.explanation: If any VA in a cluster is not connected, SailPoint makes no software or maintenance updates to any VA in that cluster. DR VAs kept in a cluster should stay running.

questions.stem: The firewall can allow outbound traffic only by IP address, not by domain name. Which VA configuration fits this restriction?
choices: HTTP proxy configuration
Standard configuration with an IP allow list of AWS endpoints
Standard configuration with inbound port 443 open
Network tunnel configuration
questions.answer: Network tunnel configuration
questions.explanation: The network tunnel option sends VA traffic to fixed regional tunnel IP addresses, designed for firewalls that cannot allow domains. Allowing the IP addresses of service endpoints is not supported.

questions.stem: Company policy requires all outbound web traffic from servers to go through a corporate proxy. Where is this configured on the VA?
choices: In hosts.yaml with the proxy server's address and port
In proxy.yaml under /home/sailpoint with https_proxy and http_proxy entries
On the cluster settings page in the Admin UI, before pairing
In static.network under the [Network] section with a Proxy line
questions.answer: In proxy.yaml under /home/sailpoint with https_proxy and http_proxy entries
questions.explanation: An HTTP proxy VA uses /home/sailpoint/proxy.yaml with https_proxy and http_proxy lines, plus proxy flags on the va-bootstrap commands. static.network holds IP settings only.

questions.stem: The corporate proxy requires NTLM authentication. What should the engineer plan for the VA?
choices: Join the VA to the domain so it can use Kerberos to the proxy
Use basic authentication in the proxy URL or let the VA through unauthenticated
Set the proxy credentials on the cluster during pairing
Enter the NTLM credentials in each source's connection settings page in the Admin UI
questions.answer: Use basic authentication in the proxy URL or let the VA through unauthenticated
questions.explanation: The VA supports only basic authentication in the proxy connection string; otherwise the proxy must let the VA through unauthenticated, for example by its IP address. Other proxy authentication methods are not supported.

questions.stem: A proxied VA must reach a locally hosted API directly for a custom connector. Which change is supported?
choices: Move the source to a cluster that uses a network tunnel
Add the host to static.network as a second gateway
Add the host to a no_proxy line in proxy.yaml
Turn the proxy off for this cluster in the Admin UI
questions.answer: Add the host to a no_proxy line in proxy.yaml
questions.explanation: proxy.yaml accepts a no_proxy line listing hosts that bypass the proxy. There is no per-cluster proxy switch in the Admin UI.

questions.stem: A security team wants VA traffic to go through both the corporate HTTP proxy and SailPoint's network tunnel. What is the problem with this design?
choices: The network tunnel works only for VAs deployed in AWS
The proxy must run on the same virtual host as the VA
The network tunnel needs outbound port 22 open to reach SailPoint's servers
The HTTP proxy option is not compatible with the network tunnel option
questions.answer: The HTTP proxy option is not compatible with the network tunnel option
questions.explanation: SailPoint documents the HTTP proxy option as incompatible with the network tunnel option, so one must be chosen. The tunnel uses outbound 443.

questions.stem: Several sources are addressed within 10.255.255.241/28, and no VA configuration can reach them. What is the cause?
choices: SailPoint reserves that range on the VA, so it does not route properly
The cluster time zone must match the subnet's data center
Standard VAs reach private ranges only through an HTTP proxy
The VA firewall blocks private ranges until a hosts.yaml entry is added for them
questions.answer: SailPoint reserves that range on the VA, so it does not route properly
questions.explanation: SailPoint reserves 10.255.255.241/28 for every VA configuration, and 172.16.0.0/22 for network tunnel VAs. Sources in those ranges need readdressing or another route.

questions.stem: An engineer must give a local VA a fixed address before pairing. Which method is documented?
choices: Create /etc/systemd/network/static.network with the NIC name, address, gateway and DNS, then reboot
Type the IP address on the Configure Virtual Appliance page
Add an ipAddress key to /home/sailpoint/config.yaml and restart
Run va-bootstrap pair with the IP address as a command option
questions.answer: Create /etc/systemd/network/static.network with the NIC name, address, gateway and DNS, then reboot
questions.explanation: Static IPs are set in a systemd static.network file using the NIC name found with ip addr, followed by a reboot. The Admin UI does not set VA addressing.

questions.stem: The company's TLS inspection appliance re-signs all outbound HTTPS traffic, and the VA now rejects the connections. Which fix is supported?
choices: Add the inspection appliance's address to hosts.yaml
Make the VA trust the organization's private root CA
Turn off certificate validation in the VA's config.yaml
Switch the VA's SailPoint traffic to plain HTTP on port 80
questions.answer: Make the VA trust the organization's private root CA
questions.explanation: VAs can be set to trust a private root CA used by deep packet inspection; otherwise they reject untrusted certificates. Disabling validation or using HTTP is not an option.

questions.stem: A firewall review asks which inbound connections a VA needs. What is the correct answer?
choices: Port 8443 from the tenant so the VA can receive updates
HTTPS on port 443 from SailPoint's cloud for job dispatch
None from SailPoint; SSH on port 22 from internal networks for administration
LDAP on port 389 from SailPoint so that it can query the company's directories
questions.answer: None from SailPoint; SSH on port 22 from internal networks for administration
questions.explanation: VA communication with SailPoint is outbound on 443; the only inbound port listed is SSH on 22, kept internal. The tenant never connects into the VA.

questions.stem: Security wants to close outbound port 123 for all VAs. What must be done first?
choices: Set the cluster's time zone on the Admin UI cluster page
Add the NTP servers to proxy.yaml as proxy exceptions
Enable debugging so that any clock drift is written to the VA logs
Configure every VA to use internal NTP servers in timesyncd.conf
questions.answer: Configure every VA to use internal NTP servers in timesyncd.conf
questions.explanation: VAs use external NTP over port 123 by default; each VA must be pointed at local NTP servers in /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf before the port can be closed. The cluster time zone only affects scheduling.

questions.stem: The firewall team asks why VAs must reach the Amazon SQS endpoints. What is the BEST explanation?
choices: The tenant uses the queue to open inbound sessions to the VA
SailPoint queues work messages there, and the VA polls them for requests
The VA uploads encrypted source credentials to the queue for long-term storage
The queue hosts the Flatcar operating system update packages
questions.answer: SailPoint queues work messages there, and the VA polls them for requests
questions.explanation: SailPoint puts messages into SQS in the tenant's region and the VA checks the queue for work. OS updates come from the Flatcar URLs.

questions.stem: A tenant is in eu-central-1, and the firewall team allowed only the Frankfurt S3, SQS and DynamoDB endpoints. What is missing?
choices: Nothing, because the region-specific endpoints are sufficient on their own
The ap-southeast-2 endpoints that receive VA log uploads
Only the identitynow.com endpoints hosted in eu-central-1
The us-east-1 endpoints for the same services must also be allowed
questions.answer: The us-east-1 endpoints for the same services must also be allowed
questions.explanation: SailPoint requires the us-east-1 URL for each listed AWS service in addition to the tenant's own region. Allowing only the local region leaves required calls blocked.

questions.stem: A VA resolves public names but cannot resolve the hostnames of internal sources. Which configuration is MOST likely missing?
choices: Internal DNS servers in the VA's network configuration
An outbound firewall rule for NTP on port 123
A cluster component that provides name resolution
A no_proxy entry for the SailPoint URLs
questions.answer: Internal DNS servers in the VA's network configuration
questions.explanation: VAs must use internal DNS servers to find internal sources, set in static.network or by DHCP. NTP and proxy settings do not affect name resolution.

questions.stem: The firewall blocks the flatcar-linux.net and flatcar-linux.org domains for VAs. What will this MOST likely affect?
choices: Pass-through authentication for Active Directory users
Generation of pairing codes during setup
Operating system security patches and updates for the VA
Connector aggregations from on-premises sources
questions.answer: Operating system security patches and updates for the VA
questions.explanation: The Flatcar URLs deliver the VA's OS security patches and updates, so blocking them leads to OS update errors. Connector work uses the SailPoint and AWS endpoints.

questions.stem: Match each VA HA/DR approach to its main characteristic.

pairs.match: No action on failover, but distant VAs may add latency
DR cluster idle until sources are repointed and credentials re-entered
Tested VAs are added to the cluster only after a disaster
Outage on the cluster whenever its VA updates and reboots

targets_extra: A load balancer spreads requests across the VAs
questions.explanation: All-running trades latency for zero-touch failover, switch clusters needs reconfiguration, and standby VAs wait to be deployed. A single VA cannot survive rolling updates; a load balancer is not needed in any design.

questions.stem: An architect must justify keeping VAs off the DMZ. Which TWO reasons does SailPoint give?
choices: The VA stores the private key that decrypts source credentials
VAs in a DMZ cannot synchronize their clocks with NTP
SailPoint Support does not accept tickets for DMZ VAs
Reaching internal sources from the DMZ means opening more internal firewall ports
VAs in a DMZ cannot reach SailPoint's cloud endpoints
answers: The VA stores the private key that decrypts source credentials
Reaching internal sources from the DMZ means opening more internal firewall ports
questions.explanation: SailPoint cites security (the credential-decrypting private key), proximity and connectivity (extra firewall openings). A DMZ VA can technically reach SailPoint, which is why the guidance is a recommendation.

questions.stem: Put the steps for giving a local VA a static IP address in order.
items: Sign in as sailpoint and change the default password
Run ip addr to find the VA's virtual NIC name
Create /etc/systemd/network/static.network with the NIC name, address, gateway and DNS
Reboot the VA with sudo reboot
Set the key passphrase and pair the VA with its cluster
questions.explanation: The NIC name is needed for the [Match] section, the file is written, and a reboot applies it. Pairing comes after the network is stable.

questions.stem: For a VA-based source, which actions are sent as requests to the source's VA cluster?
choices: Aggregation, test connection, authentication and provisioning
Search indexing, report generation and event triggers
Identity refresh, transform evaluation and role assignment
Certification generation, reviewer reminders and escalations
questions.answer: Aggregation, test connection, authentication and provisioning
questions.explanation: Any action on a VA-based source, such as aggregation, test connection, authentication or provisioning, is queued to its cluster for a VA to perform. Identity processing and campaigns run in the cloud.

questions.stem: Which VA component runs the connectors that read from and write to the organization's sources?
choices: The canal network tunnel service
The charon management service
Cloud Connector Gateway (ccg)
The systemd-timesyncd service
questions.answer: Cloud Connector Gateway (ccg)
questions.explanation: The Cloud Connector Gateway is the cluster component that runs connector operations, and its activity is in ccg.log. charon manages the VA's services and updates.

questions.stem: Right after pairing, a new VA downloads container images and starts its services. Which VA service manages this?
choices: systemd-networkd
charon
canal
ccg
questions.answer: charon
questions.explanation: charon is the VA's management service; after pairing it checks images, pulls what is missing and sets up services, which shows in charon.log. ccg is one of the services it starts.

questions.stem: An auditor asks how the SailPoint tenant gives work to an on-premises VA when the firewall allows no inbound traffic from the internet. Which answer is correct?
choices: SailPoint opens an SSH session to the VA on port 22 for each queued job
A site-to-site VPN is built between SailPoint and the customer
The tenant pushes requests to an HTTPS listener on the VA
The VA makes outbound HTTPS connections and polls for queued requests
questions.answer: The VA makes outbound HTTPS connections and polls for queued requests
questions.explanation: VAs initiate all communication outbound on 443 and pull requests queued for their cluster. No inbound internet connection or VPN is needed.

questions.stem: A team plans three sources: an on-premises Oracle HR database, a contractor list loaded by CSV upload, and a cloud app using SailPoint's SaaS connectivity. Which one needs a VA cluster?
choices: The CSV upload and the cloud app, but not the database
The contractor list, because uploaded files are parsed on a VA
The Oracle database, through the JDBC connector
The cloud app, because SaaS connectivity runs only on VAs
questions.answer: The Oracle database, through the JDBC connector
questions.explanation: Connectors that reach systems on the corporate network, such as JDBC to an internal database, run on a VA. Delimited file uploads and SaaS connectivity connectors run in SailPoint's cloud.

questions.stem: Users sign in to Identity Security Cloud with their Active Directory passwords through pass-through authentication. Where is each password checked?
choices: IQService syncs password hashes to SailPoint for comparison at sign-in
A VA in the AD source's cluster checks it against Active Directory
The tenant compares it with a password hash cached from AD
The browser sends a Kerberos ticket directly to the tenant
questions.answer: A VA in the AD source's cluster checks it against Active Directory
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication is one of the requests sent to the source's VA cluster, which binds to AD with the user's credentials. SailPoint does not hold AD password hashes.

questions.stem: A VA has just booted for the first time. How should the engineer sign in, and what must happen immediately?
choices: Sign in as sailpoint with the default password, then run passwd
Sign in with an ISC admin account, then accept the license
Sign in as admin using the pairing code, then set a password
Sign in as root with no password, then create a sailpoint user
questions.answer: Sign in as sailpoint with the default password, then run passwd
questions.explanation: The VA ships with the sailpoint user and a published default password that must be changed at once with passwd. Save the new password: losing it means building a new VA.

questions.stem: After setting the key passphrase, which command produces the code the engineer enters in the Admin UI?
choices: va-bootstrap set-passphrase
sudo systemctl start charon
sail va collect
va-bootstrap pair
questions.answer: va-bootstrap pair
questions.explanation: va-bootstrap pair displays a pairing code that is entered on the VA's page in the cluster. set-passphrase is the preceding step.

questions.stem: An engineer generated a pairing code on Friday afternoon and comes back on Monday to finish. What should the engineer do?
choices: Delete and recreate the cluster before entering any code
Run va-bootstrap pair again, because a code must be entered within 4 hours
Enter Friday's code, because codes stay valid until used
Reset the sailpoint password, then enter Friday's code
questions.answer: Run va-bootstrap pair again, because a code must be entered within 4 hours
questions.explanation: The pairing code must be entered within 4 hours, so a fresh code is needed. Recreating the cluster is unnecessary.

questions.stem: Moments after an engineer selects Pair, the new VA does not yet show Connected. What is expected?
choices: Any VA not connected within one minute must be deleted and rebuilt
A delay means the passphrase was rejected and must be set again
The status should be instant, so the VA must be rebooted at once
Setup can take about 30 minutes before the status shows Connected
questions.answer: Setup can take about 30 minutes before the status shows Connected
questions.explanation: After pairing, the VA downloads and configures its services, which takes around 30 minutes. Rebuilding or resetting it early only restarts the wait.

questions.stem: A FedRAMP customer is setting up a VA. Which command sets the key passphrase?
choices: va-bootstrap pair -t govcloud --passphrase
sudo fips-setup set-passphrase
va-bootstrap -t govcloud set-passphrase
va-bootstrap set-passphrase --fips
questions.answer: va-bootstrap -t govcloud set-passphrase
questions.explanation: FedRAMP customers add the govcloud target to the set-passphrase command. FIPS kernel mode is a separate, irreversible configuration.

questions.stem: A VA must reach SailPoint through a corporate HTTP proxy. When is the proxy configured relative to pairing?
choices: Before setting the passphrase, with proxy flags on the va-bootstrap commands
After pairing, by editing the cluster settings in the Admin UI
After the VA shows Connected, through a request to Support
During cluster creation, by selecting the proxy cluster type in the Admin UI wizard
questions.answer: Before setting the passphrase, with proxy flags on the va-bootstrap commands
questions.explanation: proxy.yaml is set first and the set-passphrase and pair commands take http and https proxy flags, because pairing itself needs the proxy. There is no proxy cluster type.

questions.stem: An organization uses only Identity Security Cloud, not IdentityIQ. Which cluster type should be selected when creating a VA cluster?
choices: Standard
Sandbox
IAI Harvester
FedRAMP
questions.answer: Standard
questions.explanation: Standard is used unless the organization has AI-Driven Identity Security for IdentityIQ, which uses IAI Harvester. The cluster type cannot be changed later.

questions.stem: An engineer adds a VA to a cluster in the Admin UI and saves it but has not yet paired the virtual machine. What is the state of that VA?
choices: It counts as a second VA and clears the Only 1 VA warning
It becomes a standby VA for disaster recovery
It immediately takes work from the cluster queue
It is saved in the cluster but is not operational until it is paired
questions.answer: It is saved in the cluster but is not operational until it is paired
questions.explanation: A new VA can be saved without pairing, but it does nothing until the virtual machine pairs with it. It cannot process requests or provide redundancy.

questions.stem: What is the keyPassphrase entered during VA setup used for?
choices: Replacing the pairing code when the VA reconnects
Generating the private key that decrypts source credentials
Encrypting the VA log files that are sent to SailPoint for support
Signing in to the VA over SSH as the sailpoint user
questions.answer: Generating the private key that decrypts source credentials
questions.explanation: Each VA holds a 2048-bit RSA private key generated from the chosen passphrase, used to decrypt credentials when talking to sources. The OS password is separate.

questions.stem: A second VA joins an existing cluster, but the engineer typed a different keyPassphrase than the first VA used. What is the MOST likely symptom?
choices: The first VA leaves the cluster and the new one takes over
Pairing fails at once with a message that the code is invalid
Its requests fail because it cannot decrypt source credentials
The new VA becomes primary and re-encrypts all credentials
questions.answer: Its requests fail because it cannot decrypt source credentials
questions.explanation: The keyPassphrase must be identical on every VA in a cluster; a mismatch gives a VA a different key, so it cannot decrypt the cluster's credentials. Only requests that VA picks up fail.

questions.stem: Which value would be accepted as a VA keyPassphrase?
choices: Harbor7/Lantern
!Harbor7Lantern
Harbor 7 Lantern
Harbor7-Lantern
questions.answer: Harbor7-Lantern
questions.explanation: The passphrase cannot start with a special character and cannot include !, /, \ or spaces. A hyphen in the middle breaks none of those rules.

questions.stem: An engineer opens /home/sailpoint/config.yaml and sees that the keyPassphrase value begins with a set of colons. What does this mean?
choices: The passphrase is empty and must be set again
The VA has automatically encrypted the passphrase
The passphrase was rejected for invalid characters
The VA is running in FIPS mode
questions.answer: The VA has automatically encrypted the passphrase
questions.explanation: The VA encrypts the keyPassphrase on its own, and encrypted values start with a leading set of colons. A plain value would mean it has not yet been encrypted.

questions.stem: No one recorded a cluster's keyPassphrase, and a new VA must be added. What is the realistic option?
choices: Run set-passphrase with any value, since the cluster adopts the newest
Reset the passphrase from the cluster's settings page in the Admin UI
Build a new cluster with a recorded passphrase, move the sources and re-enter their credentials
Ask SailPoint Support to read the passphrase back from the tenant
questions.answer: Build a new cluster with a recorded passphrase, move the sources and re-enter their credentials
questions.explanation: The passphrase is not recoverable from SailPoint and every VA in a cluster must use the same one. A new cluster, with sources moved and credentials re-entered, is the way forward.

questions.stem: A security reviewer asks where source credentials are decrypted when a connector uses them. What is the BEST answer?
choices: On the VA, with the cluster's private key, when it connects to the source
In the tenant database, which decrypts them for each connector call it makes
In the administrator's browser, which sends them with each request
On the source system, which receives them still encrypted
questions.answer: On the VA, with the cluster's private key, when it connects to the source
questions.explanation: Source credentials are protected for the VA cluster and only the VAs hold the private key that decrypts them. The cloud services never need the plaintext.

questions.stem: A source is moved from one VA cluster to another. Why must its credentials be re-entered?
choices: They are protected with the old cluster's key, which the new VAs lack
The new cluster's time zone invalidates any saved passwords
SailPoint deletes credentials whenever any source field is edited and saved
Moving a source resets it to a delimited file source
questions.answer: They are protected with the old cluster's key, which the new VAs lack
questions.explanation: Each cluster's VAs decrypt with a private key generated from that cluster's passphrase, so credentials protected for the old cluster cannot be read by the new one. SailPoint documents that switching clusters needs credentials re-entered.

questions.stem: A new cluster will hold three VAs. When is the passphrase that determines the cluster's credential key chosen?
choices: When the cluster is created, and the VAs download it from the tenant later
At each pairing, since every VA keeps an independent key
When the first VA is set up, and every later VA must use the same value
When the first source is connected, which generates the key
questions.answer: When the first VA is set up, and every later VA must use the same value
questions.explanation: The passphrase is typed on the VA with set-passphrase, not in the Admin UI, and every VA in the cluster must repeat the same value. That is why it must be recorded at the first setup.

questions.stem: The server team wants to install its antivirus and monitoring agents on every VA. What is the BEST response?
choices: Install them with the package manager and restart charon after
Install them only on one VA in each cluster to limit any risk
Install them inside the ccg container so they survive the rolling updates
Decline; the VA is a SailPoint-managed appliance with no added software
questions.answer: Decline; the VA is a SailPoint-managed appliance with no added software
questions.explanation: The VA is a hardened appliance whose OS and containers SailPoint updates; added software is unsupported and can break updates. Logs and metrics can be exported through the supported observability options instead.

questions.stem: A source's hostname is not in DNS, and the connector must reach it by name. Which change is supported on the VA?
choices: Edit /etc/hosts directly and lock the file against changes
Add an entry for the host in /home/sailpoint/hosts.yaml and restart charon
List the host in proxy.yaml so it bypasses name resolution
Put the IP address in the source's description field
questions.answer: Add an entry for the host in /home/sailpoint/hosts.yaml and restart charon
questions.explanation: SailPoint supports a hosts.yaml file in /home/sailpoint with precise indentation, applied by restarting charon. Direct edits to system files are not the supported method.

questions.stem: The infrastructure team wants to move existing VA virtual machines to a new data center. What does SailPoint advise?
choices: Move them as they are, because VAs keep no local state
Clone them into the new site and then change each clone's IP address
Build new VAs there, confirm they connect, then delete the old ones
Export config.yaml from each VA and import it into new VMs
questions.answer: Build new VAs there, confirm they connect, then delete the old ones
questions.explanation: SailPoint strongly advises against moving or migrating existing VAs. New VAs are created and connected before the old ones are deleted.

questions.stem: To save time, an administrator wants to clone a working VA to create the second VA in a cluster. What is the BEST approach instead?
choices: Clone the VA and run va-bootstrap pair on the clone only
Clone the VA and keep the clone's IP address and its configuration unchanged
Snapshot the VA and restore the snapshot onto a second host
Deploy a fresh VA image, set the same passphrase and pair it as a new VA
questions.answer: Deploy a fresh VA image, set the same passphrase and pair it as a new VA
questions.explanation: Each VA is set up from a fresh image and paired as its own VA object in the cluster. A clone would carry the original VA's identity and configuration.

questions.stem: A team enabled FIPS mode on a VA and now wants to turn it off. What must it do?
choices: Build new VAs from a fresh image, since FIPS mode cannot be reversed
Ask SailPoint Support to roll back the VA's kernel settings
Run va-bootstrap set-passphrase again without the FIPS option enabled
Disable FIPS on the cluster page in the Admin UI and restart
questions.answer: Build new VAs from a fresh image, since FIPS mode cannot be reversed
questions.explanation: FIPS is configured at the Linux kernel level on each VA and cannot be reversed or disabled. Leaving it means building new VAs.

questions.stem: The security operations team wants VA logs in its Splunk platform. Which approach is supported?
choices: Mount a network share and copy the logs over with a nightly cron job
Use the VA's log export settings to send logs to Splunk HEC
Install the Splunk universal forwarder on each VA
Ask SailPoint to open SSH so Splunk can pull the logs
questions.answer: Use the VA's log export settings to send logs to Splunk HEC
questions.explanation: SailPoint supports exporting VA logs and metrics to third-party tools such as Splunk HEC through the VA's logging configuration. Installing a forwarder is added software.

questions.stem: Which change to a VA is supported by SailPoint?
choices: Moving its operating system to a different Flatcar release channel
Adding a cron job that restarts ccg each night
Installing Python packages for custom scripts
Pointing it at internal NTP servers in timesyncd.conf
questions.answer: Pointing it at internal NTP servers in timesyncd.conf
questions.explanation: Documented changes include NTP servers, static IP, proxy, hosts.yaml and certificates. Extra packages, OS channel changes and scheduled service restarts are not supported.

questions.stem: An engineer selects Use Transport Layer Security on an Active Directory source's domain settings. What should happen to the TLS certificate?
choices: It must be installed on the administrator's workstation
It is stored on the identity profile used by the source
It should be copied to the source's VA cluster automatically
It must be emailed to SailPoint Support for installation on the VAs
questions.answer: It should be copied to the source's VA cluster automatically
questions.explanation: When TLS is enabled for a supported source, the certificate should be copied to the source's VA cluster automatically. Manual certificate placement on the VAs is the fallback.

questions.stem: Scheduled aggregations for a cluster's sources run one hour off the local time the team expects. Which setting should the engineer check?
choices: The identity profile priority
The VA cluster's time zone
The VA's NTP server list
The tenant's email locale
questions.answer: The VA cluster's time zone
questions.explanation: The cluster time zone sets the GMT offset used to schedule account and entitlement aggregations. NTP keeps the clock accurate but does not change the offset.

questions.stem: An engineer selects Enable Debugging on a VA cluster. What is the effect?
choices: Debug-level logging on all VAs in the cluster for 24 hours
Permanent verbose logging that rotates every 512 MB
Debug output written to the tenant's search index
Debug logging on one chosen VA until an administrator turns it off
questions.answer: Debug-level logging on all VAs in the cluster for 24 hours
questions.explanation: Enable Debugging turns on 24 hours of verbose logging for every VA in the cluster. Without it, log files are replaced when they reach 512 MB.

questions.stem: An engineer deletes a VA from its cluster in the Admin UI. What else must be done?
choices: Recreate the cluster so the VA count updates
Shut down the VA's virtual machine on the virtualization platform
Re-enter credentials for all sources on that cluster
Change the passphrase on the remaining VAs in the cluster
questions.answer: Shut down the VA's virtual machine on the virtualization platform
questions.explanation: Deleting the VA object does not stop the VM; leaving it running can degrade performance or cause downtime. The other VAs keep their passphrase and credentials.

questions.stem: A change board wants VA updates held until a year-end freeze ends. What is the BEST response?
choices: Pause updates for the cluster on its settings page until the freeze has ended
Open a ticket to pin the VA version for the length of the freeze
They cannot be delayed; rely on two VAs and the earlier sandbox updates
Change the cluster time zone so the update window moves out
questions.answer: They cannot be delayed; rely on two VAs and the earlier sandbox updates
questions.explanation: SailPoint manages VA updates and they cannot be skipped or delayed; sandbox usually gets them about a week before production. Two VAs per cluster keep sources available during rolling updates.

questions.stem: An engineer tries to delete the only VA in a cluster that still has sources attached, and the deletion is blocked. What should be done?
choices: Reassign those sources to a VA cluster that has working VAs
Restart the cluster and delete the VA while it reboots
Turn on debugging, then try to delete the VA again
Delete the sources first, then delete the VA
questions.answer: Reassign those sources to a VA cluster that has working VAs
questions.explanation: A VA cannot be deleted if it is the only VA in its cluster and a source still uses it. Moving the sources keeps them working; deleting them destroys data.

questions.stem: The engineer has lost the sailpoint user's OS password on one VA in a healthy cluster. What is the supported recovery?
choices: Reset the password using the cluster's keyPassphrase
Ask SailPoint Support to reset the sailpoint user's password remotely
Re-run va-bootstrap pair to receive a new password
Create a new VA in the cluster, pair it, then delete the old VA
questions.answer: Create a new VA in the cluster, pair it, then delete the old VA
questions.explanation: SailPoint states that if the sailpoint password is lost, a new VA must be created. The passphrase only protects credentials.

questions.stem: A cluster's VAs have failed to apply updates for several months. Which risk is MOST significant?
choices: Automatic deletion of the VA cluster
Loss of every source's stored credentials
Conversion of the cluster to the IAI Harvester cluster type
Loss of support, since only recent releases are supported
questions.answer: Loss of support, since only recent releases are supported
questions.explanation: Missed updates risk loss of support, missing features, open vulnerabilities and weaker high availability. Credentials and the cluster remain in place.

questions.stem: Put the steps for adding a standard VA to a new cluster in order.
items: Create the VA cluster under Admin > Connections > Virtual Appliances
Add a new VA to the cluster in the Admin UI
Start the VA image, sign in as sailpoint and change the password
Run va-bootstrap set-passphrase on the VA
Run va-bootstrap pair and enter the code in the Admin UI
Connect the cluster to a source once the VA shows Connected
questions.explanation: The cluster and VA object exist first, the VM is secured, the passphrase is set and pairing links the VM to its object. Sources are attached once the VA is connected.

questions.stem: Match each VA file to what it configures.

pairs.match: HTTP and HTTPS proxy servers and proxy exceptions
Host name entries for sources missing from DNS
Fixed IP address, gateway and DNS servers
Internal NTP servers for time synchronization
The VA's encrypted keyPassphrase and tenant settings

questions.explanation: Each file controls one supported change: proxy, host entries, addressing, time and the VA's own settings. The VA does not keep a file of cached account data for administrators to edit.

questions.stem: An engineer is documenting keyPassphrase rules for a new cluster. Which TWO statements are correct?
choices: It must be identical on every VA in the cluster
It cannot start with a special character
It can differ per VA as long as each one is recorded
It is stored only in the tenant and never on the VA
It must contain at least one space for strength
answers: It must be identical on every VA in the cluster
It cannot start with a special character
questions.explanation: Every VA in a cluster needs the same passphrase, and it cannot start with a special character or contain !, /, \ or spaces. It is kept, encrypted, in the VA's config.yaml.

questions.stem: An engineer signed in to a VA over SSH needs the service log files. In which directory are they kept?
choices: /var/log/sailpoint
/etc/sailpoint/log
/home/sailpoint/log
/opt/sailpoint/logs
questions.answer: /home/sailpoint/log
questions.explanation: VA service logs such as ccg.log and charon.log are written to /home/sailpoint/log. The other paths are common Linux conventions not used by the VA.

questions.stem: An Active Directory source's test connection fails with an LDAP error. Which VA log should the engineer read FIRST?
choices: ccg.log
charon.log
fluent.log
canal.log
questions.answer: ccg.log
questions.explanation: Connector operations such as test connection, aggregation and provisioning run in the Cloud Connector Gateway, so the details are in ccg.log. charon.log covers VA management.

questions.stem: A newly paired VA never shows a ccg container. Which log shows image checks, image pulls and service setup after pairing?
choices: canal.log
charon.log
ccg.log
worker.log
questions.answer: charon.log
questions.explanation: charon manages the VA's services and logs image checks, pulls and setup in charon.log. ccg.log cannot help when ccg is not running.

questions.stem: A VA configured with SailPoint's network tunnel cannot connect. Which log is MOST relevant?
choices: fluent.log
hosts.yaml
ccg.log
canal.log
questions.answer: canal.log
questions.explanation: canal is the VA's network tunnel service, and its activity is logged in canal.log. ccg.log covers connector operations, and hosts.yaml is not a log.

questions.stem: A provisioning failure happens only a few times a day, and the normal ccg.log entries are not detailed enough. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Enable debugging on the cluster and leave it switched on until the next quarter
Delete the VA and pair a new one to reset its log level
Enable debugging, reproduce the failure within 24 hours, then read ccg.log
Restart ccg every hour so a fresh log captures each failure
questions.answer: Enable debugging, reproduce the failure within 24 hours, then read ccg.log
questions.explanation: Debugging gives 24 hours of verbose logging across the cluster, enough to capture the issue. Leaving debug on fills the disk.

questions.stem: SailPoint Support asks for log and configuration files from both VAs in a cluster. Which SailPoint CLI command gathers them?
choices: sail va collect
sail va update
sail va parse
va-bootstrap pair
questions.answer: sail va collect
questions.explanation: sail va collect copies log and configuration files from the listed VAs to a local folder. sail va parse formats logs that were already collected.

questions.stem: An engineer has a large ccg.log file and wants only the errors in a readable format. Which command helps MOST?
choices: sudo docker images
sail va collect --config
tail -f /home/sailpoint/config.yaml
sail va parse --type ccg
questions.answer: sail va parse --type ccg
questions.explanation: sail va parse converts VA log files into readable output and shows errors by default. collect --config gathers config files only.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to confirm which containers exist on a VA and whether they are running. Which command should be used?
choices: sudo systemctl list-timers
sudo docker ps -a
timedatectl status
ip addr
questions.answer: sudo docker ps -a
questions.explanation: docker ps -a lists all containers with their status, showing whether ccg and the other services exist and are up. The other commands show timers, interfaces and time.

questions.stem: An engineer placed a source server's certificate on the VA so the connector can trust it. Which command applies it to connector operations?
choices: sudo systemctl restart ccg
sudo systemctl restart canal
va-bootstrap pair
sudo systemctl restart systemd-timesyncd
questions.answer: sudo systemctl restart ccg
questions.explanation: Connectors run in ccg, so restarting it loads newly added certificates. canal is the tunnel and timesyncd is time sync.

questions.stem: After adding a source host entry to /home/sailpoint/hosts.yaml, which command does SailPoint document to apply it?
choices: sudo systemctl restart canal
sudo systemctl restart systemd-networkd
sudo systemctl restart charon
va-bootstrap set-passphrase
questions.answer: sudo systemctl restart charon
questions.explanation: SailPoint's procedure for hosts.yaml ends with restarting charon, which applies the host entries. Restarting networkd does not read hosts.yaml.

questions.stem: The cluster shows an OS Update Warning that says a reboot is required. Which command confirms that an update is waiting for a reboot?
choices: cat /etc/os-release
timedatectl status
sudo docker images
sudo update_engine_client -status
questions.answer: sudo update_engine_client -status
questions.explanation: update_engine_client -status reports the Flatcar update state, including a status showing an update is applied and needs a reboot. /etc/os-release shows only the running version.

questions.stem: An engineer needs the VA's network interface name and current IP address before writing a static.network file. Which command shows them?
choices: timedatectl status
ip addr
sudo docker ps -a
sudo systemctl status charon
questions.answer: ip addr
questions.explanation: ip addr lists the virtual NICs and their addresses; the NIC name goes in the [Match] section. The other commands show containers, time and a service.

questions.stem: An engineer wants to watch connector activity live while running a test connection from the Admin UI. Which command is BEST?
choices: sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=1d
cat /home/sailpoint/config.yaml
tail -f /home/sailpoint/log/ccg.log
sudo docker images
questions.answer: tail -f /home/sailpoint/log/ccg.log
questions.explanation: Following ccg.log shows connector entries as the test runs. Vacuuming the journal deletes logs, the opposite of what is needed.

questions.stem: TLS errors suggest the VA's clock may be wrong. Which command shows whether the VA's clock is synchronized?
choices: ip addr
timedatectl status
sudo docker ps -a
cat /home/sailpoint/proxy.yaml
questions.answer: timedatectl status
questions.explanation: timedatectl status shows the system time and whether NTP synchronization is active. Clock drift can break TLS and token checks.

questions.stem: From the VA, an engineer wants to prove HTTPS reachability to the tenant API through the configured network path, including TLS. Which command is BEST?
choices: ip addr on the VA's external interface
ping against the tenant's api.identitynow.com host name
sudo docker images filtered for ccg
curl -v against the tenant's api.identitynow.com URL
questions.answer: curl -v against the tenant's api.identitynow.com URL
questions.explanation: curl -v shows DNS resolution, the TCP connection, the TLS handshake and the HTTP response. ping uses ICMP, often blocked, and proves nothing about HTTPS.

questions.stem: A VA reports a Disk Warning a week after an engineer investigated a source issue. What is the MOST likely cause and fix?
choices: Debug logging was left on; turn it off and clean up the logs
The disk was too small at setup; rebuild the VA at 64 GB
Aggregated account data is cached on the disk; delete the source
The OS update failed; pair the VA with the cluster again
questions.answer: Debug logging was left on; turn it off and clean up the logs
questions.explanation: A Disk Warning means file system usage is over 80%, and SailPoint first recommends turning off debug logging and clearing or splitting logs. Account data is not kept on the VA.

questions.stem: A VA shows a Memory Warning because average memory use over 12 hours is above 80%, and the team recently enabled a Data Access Security component. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Enable debugging to find which source uses the memory
Restart ccg every few hours to release the memory
Raise the VAs' memory to the minimum for the enabled components
Remove the second VA so the first one gets more host memory to use
questions.answer: Raise the VAs' memory to the minimum for the enabled components
questions.explanation: Each cluster component adds to the minimum VA size, and SailPoint recommends sizing VAs to the documented totals. Restarts only hide the problem.

questions.stem: A Service Stability Warning says a container restarted more than 10 times in 30 minutes. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Check the VA services are up to date, then restart the cluster
Disable the warning in the cluster's notification settings
Change the keyPassphrase on every VA in the cluster
Delete the container image so the VA stops restarting that container
questions.answer: Check the VA services are up to date, then restart the cluster
questions.explanation: SailPoint's guidance for repeated container restarts is to check the services are current and manually restart the cluster. Deleting images or changing keys adds new problems.

questions.stem: A VA's status badge reads VA Did Not Update. What should the engineer do FIRST?
choices: Download the latest image and upgrade the VA in place
Restart the VA cluster, and contact SailPoint Support if it persists
Disable debugging, which blocks updates while enabled
Delete the VA and remove its sources from the cluster
questions.answer: Restart the VA cluster, and contact SailPoint Support if it persists
questions.explanation: SailPoint directs a restart of the cluster for VA Did Not Update, then Support if needed. Updates are delivered by SailPoint, not by reinstalling the VA.

questions.stem: A cluster card shows the badge Only 1 VA in Cluster. What is the recommended action?
choices: Move all sources to a new cluster
Enable debugging on the existing VA
Restart the cluster to clear the badge
Add a second VA to the cluster
questions.answer: Add a second VA to the cluster
questions.explanation: SailPoint recommends at least two VAs per cluster for availability during updates. The badge is a design warning, not a fault.

questions.stem: A Certificate Expiration Warning reports that a certificate on a VA expires within 30 days. What should the engineer do?
choices: Re-pair the VA so SailPoint issues it a new certificate
Renew it in /home/sailpoint/ca-certificates/ and remove the expired one
Disable TLS on every source using the cluster
Restart the cluster so that each VA requests a new certificate from SailPoint
questions.answer: Renew it in /home/sailpoint/ca-certificates/ and remove the expired one
questions.explanation: The warning points to certificates the customer placed in /home/sailpoint/ca-certificates/; renew them there and delete or move expired ones. Disabling TLS weakens security.

questions.stem: A VA's status shows Inactive and it cannot connect, while other VAs in other clusters are fine. What is the MOST likely next step?
choices: Work with the network team to restore its outbound connectivity
Reset the keyPassphrase on that VA to a new value
Re-enter the credentials for the cluster's sources
Change the cluster type from Standard to IAI Harvester and restart it
questions.answer: Work with the network team to restore its outbound connectivity
questions.explanation: SailPoint's guidance for the Inactive state is that the VA cannot connect and the network administrator should be involved. Credentials and keys do not affect whether the VA reaches SailPoint.

questions.stem: On the VA Components tab, a process shows Busy while an update is pending. What does this mean?
choices: The process has failed and must be restarted by hand from the console
The process is locked and the VA must be rebuilt
It is working, and updates wait for a while before overriding it
The process is waiting for a new pairing code
questions.answer: It is working, and updates wait for a while before overriding it
questions.explanation: Processes report Busy to avoid disruption; idle VAs are updated first, and a continually busy process may be overridden later for critical fixes. Error, not Busy, signals a fault.

questions.stem: After a firewall change, the cluster shows a Network Error saying the VA cannot reach required endpoints. What should the engineer check FIRST?
choices: That inbound port 443 from SailPoint to the VA is open on the firewall
That debugging is enabled for the affected cluster
That the cluster time zone matches the firewall's region
That the required SailPoint and AWS URLs are allowed outbound on 443
questions.answer: That the required SailPoint and AWS URLs are allowed outbound on 443
questions.explanation: A Network Error means the VA cannot reach required endpoints, so the outbound allow list is the first check. VAs need no inbound HTTPS.

questions.stem: Outbound port 123 was blocked, and VAs now show TLS errors with a clock several minutes off. What fixes the root cause?
choices: Re-pair each VA so the tenant resets its clock
Change the VA cluster time zone to match local time
Restore NTP access or point the VAs at internal NTP servers
Enable debugging so the clock is corrected automatically
questions.answer: Restore NTP access or point the VAs at internal NTP servers
questions.explanation: Clock drift breaks TLS validation; the VA needs a working NTP source, external on 123 or internal in timesyncd.conf. The cluster time zone does not set the clock.

questions.stem: Test connection fails with an unknown host error for a source that uses a short hostname. Other sources work. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Fix the VA's DNS search domain or add a hosts.yaml entry
Open outbound port 123 for the VA's NTP traffic
Change the cluster type for the VA cluster
Re-enter the source's service account password in the source
questions.answer: Fix the VA's DNS search domain or add a hosts.yaml entry
questions.explanation: An unknown host error is name resolution; add a search domain (Domains= in static.network) or a hosts.yaml entry. Passwords and NTP do not affect resolution.

questions.stem: A JDBC source's test connection times out, while other sources on the same cluster work. What should the engineer verify?
choices: That the tenant's SQS endpoint is allowed outbound
That the VA cluster has debugging enabled for 24 hours
That the database team installed IQService on the database server
That the VAs can reach the database host on its listener port
questions.answer: That the VAs can reach the database host on its listener port
questions.explanation: Target systems have their own port needs, and a timeout on one source points to that path. SQS problems would affect every source on the cluster.

questions.stem: After the company introduced a mandatory outbound proxy, all VAs at one site lost connectivity. What is the MOST likely fix?
choices: Add the proxy server's address to hosts.yaml
Configure proxy.yaml on each VA with the proxy server and port
Open inbound port 443 from SailPoint to the VAs
Move the VAs' sources to a cluster in another region
questions.answer: Configure proxy.yaml on each VA with the proxy server and port
questions.explanation: Once direct outbound access is removed, each VA needs proxy.yaml settings to reach SailPoint. hosts.yaml only maps names to addresses.

questions.stem: A cluster uses the network tunnel configuration, and sources in 172.16.1.0/24 are unreachable from it. Standard VAs elsewhere reach them. What is the cause?
choices: Sources in private ranges need a separate cluster component
172.16.0.0/22 is reserved for network tunnel VAs, so it does not route
Network tunnel VAs can reach only sources hosted in public cloud networks
The tunnel blocks LDAP and JDBC ports by design
questions.answer: 172.16.0.0/22 is reserved for network tunnel VAs, so it does not route
questions.explanation: For network tunnel VAs, SailPoint reserves 172.16.0.0/22 in addition to 10.255.255.241/28. Sources there must be readdressed or served by a non-tunnel cluster.

questions.stem: In one cluster, test connection to a source succeeds when one VA handles it and times out when the other VA does. What should the engineer check?
choices: The source's credentials, which differ between the two VAs
The pairing code, which expired on the second VA
The second VA's network path to the source, such as firewall rules
The cluster time zone, which each VA in the cluster applies differently
questions.answer: The second VA's network path to the source, such as firewall rules
questions.explanation: Any VA in the cluster can take a request, so a timeout only via one VA points to that VA's network path. A timeout is a connectivity symptom, not a credential one.

questions.stem: Connector errors on a newly built cluster include a message that the VA cannot find the key to decrypt. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source's service account is locked in the target system
The VA's NTP server is unreachable on port 123
The cluster time zone is not set to UTC
The keyPassphrase has an unsupported character or does not match across the VAs
questions.answer: The keyPassphrase has an unsupported character or does not match across the VAs
questions.explanation: Decryption key errors usually come from a passphrase with an invalid special character or different passphrases on the VAs. Locked accounts give authentication errors instead.

questions.stem: Since a third VA joined a cluster, about one in three operations fails with decryption errors, and the failures always come from the new VA. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Rebuild the new VA with the same keyPassphrase as the other VAs
Restart the cluster so the VAs share their keys
Re-enter all source credentials so that the new VA is able to read them
Enable debugging so the new VA retries with the right key
questions.answer: Rebuild the new VA with the same keyPassphrase as the other VAs
questions.explanation: The new VA's passphrase differs, so its private key cannot decrypt the cluster's credentials. Re-entering credentials would break the original VAs instead.

questions.stem: Ten minutes after pairing, sudo docker ps -a shows no ccg container yet. What should the engineer do FIRST?
choices: Delete the VA and pair a new one at once
Install the ccg container by hand from the image
Change the passphrase and pair the VA again
Check charon.log for image pull progress and allow time for setup to finish
questions.answer: Check charon.log for image pull progress and allow time for setup to finish
questions.explanation: After pairing, charon checks and pulls images, and setup takes time, often around 30 minutes. charon.log shows progress; installing containers by hand is unsupported.

questions.stem: A long-running overnight aggregation stopped partway, and the cluster history shows a VA update at that time. What is the BEST response?
choices: Rebuild every VA in the cluster from a fresh image
Disable VA updates for the cluster so that this does not happen again
Run the aggregation again; rolling updates can interrupt running work
Move the source to a cluster with a single VA
questions.answer: Run the aggregation again; rolling updates can interrupt running work
questions.explanation: Availability is kept during rolling updates, but long processes that are still running may be interrupted. Updates cannot be disabled, and a single-VA cluster is worse.

questions.stem: The service account password for an Active Directory source was changed in AD, and aggregation now fails with an authentication error. What should the engineer do?
choices: Restart charon so the VA reads the password from AD
Update the password in the source's connection settings
Change the cluster's keyPassphrase to match the new password
Edit config.yaml on each VA with the new password
questions.answer: Update the password in the source's connection settings
questions.explanation: Source credentials are kept in the source configuration and protected for the VA cluster, so they are updated there. The VA's files and passphrase hold no source passwords.

questions.stem: A VA shows the status Configuration Incomplete after setup. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Delete this VA and set it up again
Restart charon until the status changes
Increase the VA's memory and storage
Wait 24 hours for the VA to complete automatically
questions.answer: Delete this VA and set it up again
questions.explanation: Configuration Incomplete means the VA failed to connect during configuration; SailPoint says to delete it and try again. Such VAs are often auto-deleted.

questions.stem: Match each VA log file to what it MOSTLY records.

pairs.match: Connector operations such as aggregation and test connection
VA management, image pulls and service updates

questions.explanation: ccg runs connectors, charon manages the VA, canal is the tunnel and fluent ships logs. Identity refresh happens in the cloud, not on the VA.

questions.stem: An LDAPS source fails test connection because the VA does not trust the server certificate. Put the fix in order.
items: Retrieve the server certificate with openssl s_client against the source host and port
Save the certificate as a .cer file in /home/sailpoint/certificates
Restart the connector service with sudo systemctl restart ccg
Run test connection again and review ccg.log
questions.explanation: The certificate is pulled from the server, saved where the connector service loads certificates and ccg is restarted to read it. A retest confirms the fix.

questions.stem: A VA reports a Disk Warning because file system use is over 80%. Which TWO actions does SailPoint recommend?
choices: Clear or split the VA's log files
Point the VA at an internal NTP server
Add memory to the VA
Turn off Enable Debugging on the cluster if it is not needed
Pair the VA again to reset its disk
answers: Turn off Enable Debugging on the cluster if it is not needed
Clear or split the VA's log files
questions.explanation: Disk warnings are mostly caused by logs, especially debug logs. Memory and NTP do not affect disk use, and re-pairing is not a cleanup method.
